name: Headscale
author: support@raptorpanel.net
description: A self-hosted control server for Tailscale clients, with its database in SQLite. Headscale's commands, such as creating users and keys, are typed in the console.
startup: site="{{SERVER_URL}}"; if [ -z "$site" ]; then case "${SERVER_IP:-}" in ""|0.0.0.0) site="http://localhost:{{SERVER_PORT}}" ;; *) site="http://${SERVER_IP}:{{SERVER_PORT}}" ;; esac; fi; export HEADSCALE_SERVER_URL="$site" HEADSCALE_DISABLE_CHECK_UPDATES=$([ "{{UPDATE_CHECK}}" = 1 ] && echo false || echo true); mkdir -p data; (trap - INT TERM; exec ./headscale -c config.yaml serve) & pid=$!; trap 'kill -TERM $pid 2>/dev/null; wait $pid; exit' INT TERM; echo "Type Headscale commands in the console, such as: users create alice, or: preauthkeys create --user 1"; while kill -0 $pid 2>/dev/null; do read -r -t 2 -a a; rc=$?; if [ $rc -gt 128 ]; then continue; elif [ $rc != 0 ]; then break; fi; case "${a[0]:-}" in "") ;; stop) kill -TERM $pid; break ;; headscale) ./headscale -c config.yaml "${a[@]:1}" </dev/null ;; *) ./headscale -c config.yaml "${a[@]}" </dev/null ;; esac; done; wait $pid

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# Headscale: downloads the release for the chosen version from GitHub
# (checked against GitHub's checksum) and writes a first config.yaml from
# that release's example. config.yaml, the policy and the data folder (the
# database and the server's keys) are never touched; only the program is
# replaced, once the new one has arrived.
set -euo pipefail
cd /mnt/server
work=/mnt/server/.raptor-build
rm -rf "$work" && mkdir -p "$work"
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
fail() { echo "$1"; exit 1; }
case "$(uname -m)" in
    x86_64) arch=amd64 ;;
    aarch64) arch=arm64 ;;
    *) fail "Headscale has no build for this CPU ($(uname -m))." ;;
esac

want="${VERSION:-latest}"
tag=latest
if [ "$want" != latest ]; then tag="v${want#v}"; fi
tag=$(gh-release tag juanfont/headscale "$tag") || fail "Headscale has no version $want. Set Version to latest, or to a release such as 0.29.7, then reinstall."
version="${tag#v}"

if [ -x headscale ] && ./headscale version 2>/dev/null | grep -q "version v$version$"; then
    echo "Headscale $version is already installed."
else
    echo "Downloading Headscale $version"
    gh-release download juanfont/headscale "$tag" "headscale_${version}_linux_$arch" "$work/headscale" || fail "Headscale $version has no download for this CPU."
    chmod +x "$work/headscale"
    mv -f "$work/headscale" headscale
fi

mkdir -p data
# A first configuration from Headscale's own example for this version:
# files in data/, the port Raptor gives it, metrics and the API on the
# loopback only, and no update checks (the startup sets that and the
# public address from the server's settings).
if [ ! -f config.yaml ]; then
    curl -fsSL -o "$work/config.yaml" "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/juanfont/headscale/$tag/config-example.yaml" ||
        fail "Headscale's example configuration couldn't be downloaded. Reinstall to try again."
    sed -e 's|/var/lib/headscale/|/home/container/data/|g' \
        -e 's|/var/run/headscale/headscale.sock|/home/container/data/headscale.sock|' \
        -e 's|^listen_addr: .*|listen_addr: 0.0.0.0:8080|' \
        -e 's|^disable_check_updates: .*|disable_check_updates: true|' \
        "$work/config.yaml" > config.yaml.new
    grep -q '^listen_addr: 0.0.0.0:8080$' config.yaml.new && grep -q '^unix_socket: /home/container/data/headscale.sock' config.yaml.new &&
        ! grep -q /var/lib/headscale config.yaml.new ||
        fail "Headscale's example configuration has changed shape, so config.yaml couldn't be written. Report this to Raptor."
    mv config.yaml.new config.yaml
    echo "Wrote a first config.yaml."
fi
echo "Installed Headscale $version."

variables.name: Version
variables.description: The Headscale version to install, such as 0.29.7, or latest. Reinstall to change it.

variables.name: Address
variables.description: The public address Tailscale clients connect to, starting with http or https (https behind a reverse proxy for real use). Empty uses the server's IP and port.

variables.name: Check for updates
variables.description: Let Headscale check GitHub for new versions and say so in the console.
